answer: Recurring memory-hard puzzles price every identity: each epoch, every agent must solve a fresh puzzle that needs real memory and a few minutes of compute, with the seed revealed only at epoch start so no work can be stockpiled. One honest agent pays this once, but a sybil farm must forge a new solution for every fake, every epoch, so its hardware bill grows linearly with its size. A clever sonnet or a fine quill of prose earns nothing for an identity that skips the puzzle; it simply drops out of the reward set.
